# GenericTensor0D

> Create a "generic" zero-dimensional [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor].

<!-- Section to include introductory text. Make sure to keep an empty line after the intro `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<!-- Package usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var GenericTensor0D = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/tensor0d/generic' );
```

#### GenericTensor0D( value\[, options] )

Creates a "generic" zero-dimensional [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] from a scalar value.

```javascript
var arr = new GenericTensor0D( 1.0 );
// returns <ndarray>[ 1.0 ]
```

The function accepts the following options:

-   **order**: specifies whether an [ndarray][@stdlib/ndarray/ctor] is `'row-major'` (C-style) or `'column-major'` (Fortran-style). Default: `'row-major'`.
-   **readonly**: boolean indicating whether an array should be **read-only**. Default: `false`.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<!-- Package usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var discreteUniform = require( '@stdlib/random/base/discrete-uniform' );
var map = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/map' );
var GenericTensor0D = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/tensor0d/generic' );

// Create a zero-dimensional ndarray containing a random value:
var x = new GenericTensor0D( discreteUniform( 1, 100 ) );
console.log( x.get() );

// Define a function which applies a threshold:
function threshold( v ) {
    return ( v > 10 ) ? v : 0;
}

// Apply threshold:
var y = map( x, threshold );
console.log( y.get() );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
